Water leaves cells by osmosis because the external solution has lower water potential.
Unremoved surface liquid adds variable mass unrelated to water movement in the tissue.
One tuber does not estimate between-plant variation, limiting generalization.
Water molecules continue crossing both ways at equal average rates.
